question:
A customer reports a defect in the executable we shipped to them two years ago, and to investigate it we need that very same executable back, byte for byte, but the toolchain and third-party libraries on our machines have been upgraded since then. What should the team have been tracking and preserving so that this would be possible?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

To reproduce a shipped executable byte-for-byte after toolchain upgrades, teams must place all build inputs—source code, build tools (compilers, linkers), third-party libraries, build instructions, and configuration data—under SCM control, maintain baselines, and preserve the ability to reproduce previous releases.

# Guidelines

- Place supporting tools (e.g., compilers) under SCM control so that correct tool versions are available to rebuild any previously built software configuration item. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt e082f1c815b2042b56a6].")

- Maintain build instructions under SCM control and ensure they are followed in the correct sequence when reproducing a build. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 1e8d66262f1680402200].")

- SCM must [SWEBOK excerpt 413ba3a4edd1bb80a345]. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt ed245abb0f39c360af98].")

- Use version control tools to track, document, and store all configuration items including source code and external documentation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Management Tools and Verification Activities.md)

- Identify and control all software items with potential to become SCIs, including source and executable code, software tools, plans, specifications, testing materials, and libraries. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt d4b749f5ec14b5d06a14].")

- Use a repository to store binaries created during the build process so that build artifacts can be retrieved and redeployed as required during the release verification process. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 93cb0cdc79d239bdea25].")

- Plan for vendor/subcontractor control by tracking purchased software products such as compilers and other tools, and manage how their changes or updates are evaluated. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 1801fc66e493feebf0ab].")

- Produce and preserve a version description document (VDD) recording the physical contents of each release, including which variants of items were selected. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 1bc7457ba6b688fca089]).")

- Produce and preserve a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) listing the artifacts included in each build as an important CM output. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 450578f233490c4cd9fa].")

- Preserve build outputs as records of quality, security, or compliance, since they may be needed for future reference. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt a35fff3110753b6e55b1].")

- Track which approved software change requests [SWEBOK excerpt 61550993d22c360bca4b], so the exact content of any release can be reconstructed. (source: "[SWEBOK excerpt 3d4584821b2c458b42e8].")

- Include [SWEBOK excerpt c4e1be1200adcea889ba]—in the SCM plan to ensure they remain available throughout the software lifecycle. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Plan Development.md)
